currentContext.strengths: Market leadership in core categories: #1 in Fans and #1 in Residential Pumps, #3 in Storage Water Heaters, #6 in Air Coolers, #3 in B2C lighting|Butterfly holds #1 brand position in LPG stainless steel gas stoves (PAN-India), #2 in LPG gas stoves and outer-lid pressure cookers, #2 in mixer grinders (South)|'World's number one ceiling fans' claim converted into an end-to-end on-pack, print and retail campaign, reinforcing consumer trust|Zero debt and net cash positive status providing resilience and financial flexibility|Extensive multi-channel distribution: 2,76,000+ retailers, 7,000+ channel partners and 1,300+ authorised service centres across urban, semi-urban and rural markets|Platform-first innovation strategy with an annual allocation of up to INR 100 Crore, scaling high-efficiency BLDC motor technology (SilentPro) across the fan portfolio|Consumer-insight-led design contributing to lower product return rates and high satisfaction|85+ year legacy and award-winning products, including the India Design Mark Award 2025 for Flame Pro Cooktop|Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025 (Consumer Appliances Sector) from the Institute of Directors, London|Lighting segment achieved industry-leading margins by shifting from commoditised categories to premium consumer lighting and high-value B2B projects|Early-mover position in decentralised solar: market leadership in solar pumps and an emerging residential rooftop solar presence
currentContext.strategies: Crompton 2.0 transformation as the organising strategic framework for the Company|Protect and grow the core (fans, pumps and the established consumer electricals portfolio)|Win in the kitchen (kitchen and cooking appliances, including the Butterfly portfolio)|Foray into new segments (new business platforms beyond the established core)|Transform the lighting business away from commoditised categories|Premiumisation of the portfolio, with focus on aesthetics, smarter functionality and refined user experience|Consumer need-led innovation as a growth enabler|Go-to-market excellence and supply chain excellence as operating enablers|Digital enablement across the organisation|Building an enabled and empowered organisation|Leveraging the 'World's No. 1 ceiling fans' brand position as a consumer-facing trust asset|Integrated reporting through a multiple-capital lens with strategy as the organising reference|The routed governance sections describe capital allocation as a Board-level responsibility rather than a numeric policy: the Board is responsible for developing strategy, overseeing material acquisitions and divestments, managing capital expenditure and the Company's capital structure, and handling other financing matters, and it oversees significant capital expenditures, acquisitions, mergers and other strategic initiatives essential to long-term success. This is codified through a Board-approved suite of statutory and non-statutory codes and policies that governs how capital and risk are handled, including the Dividend Distribution Policy, Investment Policy, Policy on Foreign Exchange Risk Management, Risk Management Policy, Materiality Policy, Policy on Materiality and Dealing with Related Party Transactions, Policy for Determining Material Subsidiary and Corporate Social Responsibility Policy. The Board frames itself as trustee of shareholders' capital and commits to enhancing shareholder value while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders. Statutorily mandated community reinvestment runs through the CSR framework, built on the principles of 'Responsible Business' and 'Shared Value' with an obligation set at two percent of average net profit under Section 135 and oversight by a reconstituted CSR Committee chaired by an Independent Director. Form AOC-1 Part B confirms the Company has no associates or joint ventures, none yet to commence operations and none liquidated or sold during the year, so there is no associate/JV capital deployed.|Zero waste to landfill commitment maintained across operations|Zero non-conformities in ISO surveillance audits|Environmental sustainability framework built on three areas: products, infrastructure facilities and the supply chain, to reduce lifecycle impact and improve resource efficiency|Development of BEE star-rated fans and water heaters as a stated product-sustainability priority|Solar pump systems as a decarbonisation-linked product priority|Product carbon footprint assessments and GreenPro-aligned product development|Energy conservation and renewable energy adoption at manufacturing facilities|Water stewardship and waste reduction at facilities, with continued recycling and reuse initiatives|Regular environmental monitoring and tracking of air, water and noise parameters|Centralised ESG management software and environmental performance dashboard providing audit-ready tracking of energy, water, waste and emissions across the value chain|Investment in advanced laboratories and testing capability including NVH testing, RoHS compliance, packaging performance testing and EMI/EMC validation|Responsible supply chain as a stated pillar, with rigorous vendor onboarding and supplier quality programmes|Employee well-being architecture: 'Happy to Help' assistance programme, women's safety workshops, SpeakUp platform and HRBP-led psychological safety|Leadership and capability building through CLDP, FLDP, ELDP, Grow with Crompton and the Belt Certification Model|Risk governance structure comprising the Board Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee, Enterprise Risk Management Committee (bi-annual risk reviews) and the Risk Council
currentContext.expansion: The sections of the FY2025-26 Integrated Annual Report routed to this domain do not disclose any specific Crompton plant, production line or capacity-expansion project with a named capex value, commissioning date or ramp timeline. The MD&A content routed here is industry-level opportunity sizing rather than company capex: it describes structural runways in lighting (industry estimated at ~$4.9 billion in 2026 growing to ~$6.9 billion by 2031 at ~7.2% CAGR), large kitchen appliances ($2.37 billion in 2025 to $7.23 billion by 2035 at an 11.8% CAGR), small domestic appliances, wires and cables (~$21 billion in 2025 to ~$35.6 billion by 2031 at ~9% CAGR, with the organised segment now ~70% of housing wires), and solar (India rooftop solar cumulative capacity ~13.7 GW in 2024 projected to grow at ~28% CAGR to ~167 GW by 2034, near-term 25-30 GW by FY27, and PM-KUSUM targeting ~35 lakh solar pumps against a national 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030). On the funding side, the Board's Report states the Company was debt-free as on March 31, 2026, with principal liquidity from cash and cash equivalents, liquid investments and operating cash flow, and a robust working-capital management process; the Company holds credit ratings from CRISIL Ratings Limited and India Ratings and Research Private Limited (the rating table is truncated in the routed text). The only share-capital movement during the year was the allotment of 1,05,712 equity shares on exercise of options under the Crompton Employee Stock Option Scheme 2016, with no change in authorised capital and no shares with differential rights or sweat equity issued.

risks.note: Named by management as a key focus area of the Enterprise Risk Management framework. Crompton's core categories are directly exposed to BEE star-rating and efficiency labelling changes, and product roadmaps (BEE star-rated fans and water heaters) must be re-engineered whenever norms tighten.

Explicitly listed among the key risk focus areas. Quality failures would hit brand trust and warranty cost, which is why the Company embeds quality via the SAP Quality Module, stage-gate NPD validation, reliability testing, plant and supplier Kaizens and QC Story defect-reduction projects.

Flagged as a key ERM focus area. Exposure spans decarbonisation, resource efficiency, responsible product design, zero waste to landfill and monitoring of air, water and noise parameters across facilities and the supply chain, with regulatory and reputational consequences if standards slip.

Listed as a key risk focus area. Growth depends on proprietary platforms NUCLEUS (premium efficiency and BLDC-led participation) and XTECH (reliability and durability); failure to keep translating consumer insight into differentiated products would erode premiumisation and category leadership.

Named among key risk focus areas. As purchase decisions shift toward experience, after-sales support and brand credibility, weak service delivery across the retailer and service network directly threatens brand salience and repeat demand.

Management states it tracks and mitigates risks across product, brand and operational areas. Brand Crompton is the central asset behind premiumisation and go-to-market excellence, so dilution of brand salience is treated as a tracked enterprise risk.

risks.risk: Supply-chain planning, stock-out and excess-inventory risk
risks.note: Management identifies inventory discipline as a risk to be managed, addressed through Project ForeSight digital forecast enrichment to align production schedules with demand, standardised SOPs, rigorous vendor onboarding, Butterfly warehouse integration and QR-code Track-and-Trace across all product lines and 30 warehouses.

The cautionary statement warns that expectations about future events and operating performance rest on assumptions subject to inherent risks and uncertainties, and that actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied.

one-line thesis: Crompton delivered robust Q4 growth (11% YoY revenue, 14% lighting growth) driven by BLDC fan leadership, solar rooftop scaling (5,000+ installations), and Butterfly’s double-digit recovery, while margin expansion to 11.9% EBITDA reflected disciplined pricing and cost optimization — what matters is the strategic pivot to premiumization via Rhion and scalable new businesses (solar, wires) with strong ROCE, positioning Crompton as a multi-category consumer energy transition leader.
financial scorecard: revenue: +11% YoY to Rs.2,283 Cr; EBITDA/margin: +11.9% (up from 6.8% in H1); PAT (rptd): impacted by Rs.170 Cr Butterfly impairment; PAT (normalized): +15% YoY excluding impairment; order book: Rs.500 Cr solar rooftop (38,000 units), solar pumps growing >100% YoY; net debt: net cash positive (Crompton + Butterfly combined cash Rs.170 Cr)
guidance: revenue growth: target Rs.2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years; margin: sustain 10%+ EBITDA as pricing offsets inflation; order inflow: solar rooftop execution accelerating; capex/commissioning: minimal new capex, leveraging existing infrastructure for solar/wires rollout
order book & pipeline: Rs.500 Cr solar rooftop order book (38,000 units across Andhra & Telangana); 5,000+ homes installed; solar pumps revenue >Rs.200 Cr (doubled from prior year); wires order book not disclosed but national rollout imminent
segment / subsidiary detail: ECD: 10% growth led by SDA (+30% Q4, driven by air fryers/infrared cooktops), BLDC fans (+30%+), pumps (residential share stable, agri + teens); Lighting: 14% growth, B2B shifted to higher-margin commercial, B2C moved to panels/floodlights; Butterfly: 17% revenue growth, EBIT margins stable, cash flow positive; Solar Rooftop: 5,000+ homes installed, order book Rs.500 Cr; Wires: launched as Crompton Armor in South, national rollout planned; LDA: water heater market share #2, air cooler inventory cleared
growth verticals / optionality: Rhion super-premium PL (new product line for cutting-edge design tech); national rollout of wires; Butterfly expansion into NEW markets; solar pumps & rooftop scaling to Rs.2,000 Cr business in 3-4 years; potential integration of LKA into Rhion
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% in Q4 from 6.8% in H1 via pricing (7-8% cumulative in fans), cost optimization (Unnati), and operating leverage; raw material inflation (post-war) partially offset by pricing; Butterfly facing similar inflation but passing on costs; no margin compression expected post-inflation normalization
capex / expansion: minimal new capex; leveraging existing manufacturing (Baroda, Baddi) and distribution; solar/wires rollout uses existing channel; no major greenfield capex disclosed
capital allocation: dividend maintained at prior year level; Rs.170 Cr Butterfly cash now net positive; Rs.100 Cr/year invested in R&D/innovation; impairment of Butterfly non-cash; focus on organic growth over M&A; Rhion PL funded internally
risks & watch-items: geopolitical-driven input cost volatility; delayed competitor price responses; solar rooftop execution delays; BEE 2.0 water heater compliance cost pass-through risk; channel financing exposure in solar (minimal); consumer demand elasticity in premium segments
management quality / tone: confident, execution-focused, and forward-looking; emphasized premiumization, margin discipline, and strategic clarity; acknowledged inflation but projected industry leadership; tone on Butterfly shifted from turnaround to growth engine; Rhion launch framed as culmination of 3-4 years of innovation
non-obvious takeaways: Butterfly’s Rs.170 Cr cash position and net cash positivity is a hidden asset; Rhion’s EBO/MBO channel leverage from Butterfly’s existing infrastructure; solar rooftop order book is 10x installed base, indicating massive future revenue visibility; BEE 2.0 fan transition was a hidden catalyst for BLDC adoption; Crompton’s 70+ EBOs are an underappreciated premium distribution moat

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

hero.oneLiner: Crompton is a leading Indian consumer durables and lighting company with market leadership in fans and residential pumps and a strong position in lighting and appliances, built on an 85+ year legacy and a PAN-India distribution network.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Crompton is a leading Indian consumer durables and lighting company with market leadership in fans and residential pumps and a strong position in lighting and appliances, built on an 85+ year legacy and a PAN-India distribution network.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Crompton designs and sells consumer electrical products across fans, pumps, lighting and appliances, serving households, farmers and institutions through an extensive multi-channel PAN-India network of retailers, channel partners and authorised service centres. Its portfolio spans Electrical Consumer Durables (fans, residential/agricultural/solar pumps, water heaters, air coolers, small domestic appliances and large kitchen appliances), B2C and B2B lighting, and the Butterfly kitchen-appliance business. Through its Crompton 2.0 transformation the Company is advancing consumer-centric innovation, portfolio premiumisation and go-to-market capability while building new growth engines in integrated solar solutions and wires and cables.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: ECD: 10% growth led by SDA (+30% Q4, driven by air fryers/infrared cooktops), BLDC fans (+30%+), pumps (residential share stable, agri + teens); Lighting: 14% growth, B2B shifted to higher-margin commercial, B2C moved to panels/floodlights; Butterfly: 17% revenue growth, EBIT margins stable, cash flow positive; Solar Rooftop: 5,000+ homes installed, order book Rs.500 Cr; Wires: launched as Crompton Armor in South, national rollout planned; LDA: water heater market share #2, air cooler inventory cleared

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Electrical Consumer Durables (ECD):** Ceiling fans, Pedestal, table and wall-mounted fans, Exhaust fans, BLDC fans (SilentPro), Residential pumps, Agricultural pumps, Solar pumps, Dura series V3 and V4 submersibles, Aquagold, Flomax Dura, SWJ, Monoblock and open well pumps, Smart controllers and MNRE-compliant solar pump solutions, Water heaters (Solarium Blaze), Immersion Rods, Oil-Filled Radiators, Air coolers, Irons, Mixer grinders, Juicers and blenders, Induction cooktops, Chimneys (including India's first AQI-based chimney), Flame Pro Cooktop
- **Lighting:** B2C ceiling lights, Lamps, Battens, Street lights, Flood lights, Lighting accessories, B2B street, flood, industrial, professional and infrastructure lighting
- **Butterfly:** Mixer grinders, Pressure cookers, Gas stoves, Chimneys, Hobs, Cookware, Other kitchen appliances, 'Idea First' premium series
- **New Businesses:** Solar rooftop solutions, Wires and cables, Crompton Armor Wires

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian households (urban, semi-urban and rural)
- Farmers and agricultural water management
- Institutional and B2B lighting projects (street, industrial, professional, infrastructure)
- Residential rooftop solar customers
- PAN-India general trade, modern trade and e-commerce channels
- Export markets (export business grew during the year)

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- CII GreenPro Ecolabel for the entire B2B lighting product range (first lighting company to receive it)
- 100% RoHS-compliant lighting product designs
- BEE 2.0 energy ratings transition completed for ceiling fans
- BIS requirements implemented in Air Coolers
- MNRE-compliant solar pump solutions
- ISO 9001:2015 certification for the Corporate Secretarial function from Bureau Veritas - UKAS Management Systems

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Rs.500 Cr solar rooftop order book (38,000 units across Andhra & Telangana); 5,000+ homes installed; solar pumps revenue >Rs.200 Cr (doubled from prior year); wires order book not disclosed but national rollout imminent

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: target Rs.2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years; margin: sustain 10%+ EBITDA as pricing offsets inflation; order inflow: solar rooftop execution accelerating; capex/commissioning: minimal new capex, leveraging existing infrastructure for solar/wires rollout

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Rhion super-premium PL (new product line for cutting-edge design tech); national rollout of wires; Butterfly expansion into NEW markets; solar pumps & rooftop scaling to Rs.2,000 Cr business in 3-4 years; potential integration of LKA into Rhion

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- BEE-linked efficiency norms and rising consumer awareness are supporting a shift toward BLDC and premium decorative fan variants
- BLDC fans are among the fastest-growing sub-segments; BLDC-powered fans consume up to 50-65% less energy than conventional models
- Indian electric fan market reached $2 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to $5.64 billion by 2033 at a 12.2% CAGR
- Pump demand is anchored in residential water management, agriculture, construction activity and retail replacement, with long-term support from solar pump adoption under PM-KUSUM
- Pumps are seeing a technology and premiumisation shift toward smart, IoT-enabled and solar-compatible products with dry-run protection and remote monitoring
- Water heaters and air coolers benefit from low penetration, climate-linked demand, compact urban living and rising preference for smart, safe and energy-efficient appliances
- Water heater demand is shifting toward instant and storage units with improved design, enhanced safety features and lower operating costs
- Lighting demand is supported by LED replacement, infrastructure upgrades and public energy-efficiency programmes; the industry is estimated at ~$4.9 billion in 2026 and projected to reach ~$6.9 billion by 2031 at ~7.2% CAGR
- Smart and connected lighting (IoT bulbs, app-controlled systems, sensors, tunable lighting) is growing meaningfully faster than the broader lighting market
- B2B and project lighting is gaining traction from smart cities, highways, industrial corridors, retail, warehousing and commercial real estate
- Wires are gaining from housing, renovation, safety awareness and the shift toward organised branded products
- PM Surya Ghar is encouraging household rooftop solar adoption, moving policy support closer to Crompton's demand pools
- General trade continues to dominate electrical goods, while modern trade, e-commerce and assisted digital discovery expand access to premium and new-age categories, especially in Tier II and III markets
- Brand credibility, service assurance and portfolio relevance are becoming key differentiators as consumers compare features, lifecycle cost, energy savings and after-sales support
- The induction fan segment benefits from a highly localised and mature domestic supply chain, supporting cost competitiveness and reducing import dependence
- Near-term performance may continue to be influenced by commodity-price volatility, weather-linked seasonality and uneven discretionary demand
- Lighting near-term demand may be influenced by commodity volatility, channel destocking and pricing pressures in commoditised LED categories
- Medium-term industry outlook remains constructive, supported by India's expanding consumption base, home improvement trends and energy-efficiency awareness
- Macro backdrop: India's growth strengthened to 7.2% in FY26 per the World Bank, with the Economic Survey 2025-26 projecting FY27 growth at 6.8%-7.2%
- Consumption sentiment benefited from income tax relief and selective GST rationalisation; rural demand is expected to recover and urban consumption to benefit from wage growth and premiumisation

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% in Q4 from 6.8% in H1 via pricing (7-8% cumulative in fans), cost optimization (Unnati), and operating leverage; raw material inflation (post-war) partially offset by pricing; Butterfly facing similar inflation but passing on costs; no margin compression expected post-inflation normalization

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: dividend maintained at prior year level; Rs.170 Cr Butterfly cash now net positive; Rs.100 Cr/year invested in R&D/innovation; impairment of Butterfly non-cash; focus on organic growth over M&A; Rhion PL funded internally

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The sections of the FY2025-26 Integrated Annual Report routed to this domain do not disclose any specific Crompton plant, production line or capacity-expansion project with a named capex value, commissioning date or ramp timeline. The MD&A content routed here is industry-level opportunity sizing rather than company capex: it describes structural runways in lighting (industry estimated at ~$4.9 billion in 2026 growing to ~$6.9 billion by 2031 at ~7.2% CAGR), large kitchen appliances ($2.37 billion in 2025 to $7.23 billion by 2035 at an 11.8% CAGR), small domestic appliances, wires and cables (~$21 billion in 2025 to ~$35.6 billion by 2031 at ~9% CAGR, with the organised segment now ~70% of housing wires), and solar (India rooftop solar cumulative capacity ~13.7 GW in 2024 projected to grow at ~28% CAGR to ~167 GW by 2034, near-term 25-30 GW by FY27, and PM-KUSUM targeting ~35 lakh solar pumps against a national 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030). On the funding side, the Board's Report states the Company was debt-free as on March 31, 2026, with principal liquidity from cash and cash equivalents, liquid investments and operating cash flow, and a robust working-capital management process; the Company holds credit ratings from CRISIL Ratings Limited and India Ratings and Research Private Limited (the rating table is truncated in the routed text). The only share-capital movement during the year was the allotment of 1,05,712 equity shares on exercise of options under the Crompton Employee Stock Option Scheme 2016, with no change in authorised capital and no shares with differential rights or sweat equity issued.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: confident, execution-focused, and forward-looking; emphasized premiumization, margin discipline, and strategic clarity; acknowledged inflation but projected industry leadership; tone on Butterfly shifted from turnaround to growth engine; Rhion launch framed as culmination of 3-4 years of innovation

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "The Board's Report states there are no proceedings, either filed by the Company or against the Company, pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 before the NCLT or other courts during F.Y. 2025-26, and that no fraud has been reported by the Auditors to the Audit Committee or the Board.", "as_of": "2026-07-08"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership in core categories: #1 in Fans and #1 in Residential Pumps, #3 in Storage Water Heaters, #6 in Air Coolers, #3 in B2C lighting
- Butterfly holds #1 brand position in LPG stainless steel gas stoves (PAN-India), #2 in LPG gas stoves and outer-lid pressure cookers, #2 in mixer grinders (South)
- 'World's number one ceiling fans' claim converted into an end-to-end on-pack, print and retail campaign, reinforcing consumer trust
- Zero debt and net cash positive status providing resilience and financial flexibility
- Extensive multi-channel distribution: 2,76,000+ retailers, 7,000+ channel partners and 1,300+ authorised service centres across urban, semi-urban and rural markets
- Platform-first innovation strategy with an annual allocation of up to INR 100 Crore, scaling high-efficiency BLDC motor technology (SilentPro) across the fan portfolio
- Consumer-insight-led design contributing to lower product return rates and high satisfaction
- 85+ year legacy and award-winning products, including the India Design Mark Award 2025 for Flame Pro Cooktop
- Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025 (Consumer Appliances Sector) from the Institute of Directors, London
- Lighting segment achieved industry-leading margins by shifting from commoditised categories to premium consumer lighting and high-value B2B projects
- Early-mover position in decentralised solar: market leadership in solar pumps and an emerging residential rooftop solar presence

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: geopolitical-driven input cost volatility; delayed competitor price responses; solar rooftop execution delays; BEE 2.0 water heater compliance cost pass-through risk; channel financing exposure in solar (minimal); consumer demand elasticity in premium segments

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Butterfly’s Rs.170 Cr cash position and net cash positivity is a hidden asset; Rhion’s EBO/MBO channel leverage from Butterfly’s existing infrastructure; solar rooftop order book is 10x installed base, indicating massive future revenue visibility; BEE 2.0 fan transition was a hidden catalyst for BLDC adoption; Crompton’s 70+ EBOs are an underappreciated premium distribution moat

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Crompton 2.0 transformation as the organising strategic framework for the Company
- Protect and grow the core (fans, pumps and the established consumer electricals portfolio)
- Win in the kitchen (kitchen and cooking appliances, including the Butterfly portfolio)
- Foray into new segments (new business platforms beyond the established core)
- Transform the lighting business away from commoditised categories
- Premiumisation of the portfolio, with focus on aesthetics, smarter functionality and refined user experience
- Consumer need-led innovation as a growth enabler
- Go-to-market excellence and supply …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Industry outlook] The deck cites a projected consumer durables market size of INR 3 trillion by FY29, 11% CAGR growth for the Indian consumer durable sector by 2029, 4th largest global market by 2027 and 0.9% contribution to GDP by 2027 (source: Industry Reports, IBEF).
- [Regulation] Two regulatory shifts are flagged as shaping 2026: the "BEE Ratings Upgrade", which raises manufacturing standards and is expected to "compel brands to invest in engineering and product-lifecycle practices", and "EPR Mechanisms" creating "a reverse ecosystem for sustainable, compliant product design".
- [Exceptional item] The deck's own financial tables carry an exceptional item of 716 (Rs. Cr) in the Q4 FY26 comparative column (nil in Q1 FY27 and Q1 FY26); the deck gives no explanation of what it relates to.
- [Marketing scale] Fans summer campaign reported at 80 Mn+ TV reach across 50+ channels, 52 Mn+ digital reach, 100+ billboards across 16 cities, 95 bus wraps, and 6 AI-powered in-house cricket micro-dramas with 38M+ views; Dainik Bhaskar SuperChef ran across 11 states with 36,000+ entries.
- [Awards] "Learning Reimagined Excellence of the Year 2026" award at the GEEF Global Awards.
